facts.text: Vedic religion, Jainism, Buddhism, Judaism, Christianity, Islam and Zoroastrianism have been important in India; Sikhism was established in the medieval period.
facts.quote: Religious trends such as Vedic religion, Jainism, Buddhism, Judaism, Christianity, Islam and Zoroastrianism have been important in the Indian religious fabric. In the medieval period Sikhism was established.

facts.text: Inclusiveness is an integral quality of Indian culture; it has helped to maintain unity in diversity.
facts.quote: Inclusiveness is an integral quality of Indian culture. This quality has helped to maintain unity in diversity in our country.

facts.text: The Vedic religion is based on Shruti (the Vedas), Smriti (Vedic literature) and Puranas.
facts.quote: The Vedic religion is based on Shruti (The Vedas), Smriti (Vedic literature) and Puranas.

facts.text: Christianity and Judaism arrived in India during the 1st century CE; followers of Islam and Zoroastrianism arrived approximately in the 7th and 8th century CE.
facts.quote: Christianity and Judaism arrived in India during the 1st Century CE. Followers of Islam and Zoroastrianism arrived in India approximately in the 7th & 8th Century CE.

facts.text: The Vedic religion is considered the oldest religion in India; Vedic people performed Yajnas and worshipped nature.
facts.quote: The Vedic religion is considered to be the oldest religion in India. Vedic literature is the basis of this religion. The Vedic people performed sacrifices (Yajnas) and worshipped nature.

facts.text: The basic texts of the Vedic religion include the Vedas, Upanishads, Puranas and Dharmashastras.
facts.quote: The basic texts of the Vedic religion include the Vedas, Upanishads, Puranas, and Dharmashastras.

facts.text: The two sutras: Aham Brahmasmi - I am Brahman; Tat Tvam Asi - You are that.
facts.quote: Aham Brahmasmi - I am Brahman. Tat Tvam Asi - You are that.

facts.text: Hinduism is an extended form of the Vedic religion; in Hinduism a person's destiny is believed to be determined by Karma (behaviour and actions).
facts.quote: Hinduism is an extended form of the Vedic religion. ... In Hinduism, it is believed that an individual's destiny is determined by his/her Karma (behaviour and actions).

facts.text: Dharma means observing values like truth, morality, fulfilment of duty and social service.
facts.quote: Observing values like truth, morality, the fulfillment of duty and social service makes up an individual's inherent Dharma.

facts.text: The Bhagavad Gita, a sacred text of the Hindus, instructs that everyone should perform their duties without a thought to the outcome.
facts.quote: The 'Bhagavad Gita' is a sacred text of the Hindus. It instructs that every individual should perform their respective duties without a thought to the outcome.

facts.text: Adya Shankaracharya lived in the 8th century CE, stressed knowledge and renunciation and wrote commentaries on the Upanishads, Brahma Sutras and Bhagavad Gita.
facts.quote: Adya Shankaracharya lived in the 8th century CE. He put great emphasis on knowledge and renunciation. He wrote commentaries on texts like the 'Upanishads', the 'Brahma Sutras' and the 'Bhagavad Gita'.

facts.text: Adya Shankaracharya established four Muths at Badrinath, Dwarka, Jagannathpuri and Shringeri.
facts.quote: He established four Muths in the four cardinal directions of India at Badrinath, Dwarka, Jagannathpuri and Shringeri.

facts.text: 'Sarve bhavantu sukhinah' means 'May everyone be happy'.
facts.quote: Sarve bhavantu sukhinah : May everyone be happy.

facts.text: The six schools of Indian philosophy are the Shaddarshanas: Samkhya, Yoga, Nyaya, Vaisheshika, Purva Mimamsa and Vedanta; 'Darshana' means 'Philosophy'.
facts.quote: These are collectively known as the 'Shaddarshanas' ... The term 'Darshana' means 'Philosophy.' The Shaddarshanas consist of six distinct schools: Samkhya, Yoga, Nyaya, Vaisheshika, Purva Mimamsa and Vedanta.

facts.text: Samkhya Darshana explains the creation of the universe.
facts.quote: Samkhya Darshana : This school gives an explanation regarding the creation of the universe.

facts.text: Yoga Darshana stresses self-realisation through spiritual discipline (Sadhana) and meditation (Dhyan).
facts.quote: Yoga Darshana : This school gives importance to attainment of self-realization through continuous practice of spiritual discipline (Sadhana) and meditation (Dhyan)

facts.text: Nyaya Darshana is based on Logic and Epistemology (the theory of knowledge).
facts.quote: Nyaya Darshana : This school is based on the principles of Logic and Epistemology (the theory of knowledge).

facts.text: Vaisheshika Darshana holds that the entire universe is composed of atoms.
facts.quote: Vaisheshika Darshana : The core principle of this school is the theory that the entire universe is composed of atoms.

facts.text: Purva Mimamsa Darshana analyses the rites and rituals prescribed in the Vedas.
facts.quote: Purva Mimamsa Darshana : This school analyses the rites and rituals prescribed in the Vedas.

facts.text: Vedanta Darshana is based on the philosophical teachings of the Upanishads.
facts.quote: Vedanta Darshana : This school is based on the philosophical teachings of the Upanishads.

facts.text: Jainism stresses non-violence (Ahimsa); there have been 24 Tirthankars and Vardhaman Mahavir is the twenty-fourth.
facts.quote: This religion gives importance to the principle of non-violence (Ahimsa). ... There have been 24 Tirthankars in all. Vardhaman Mahavir is the twenty- fourth Tirthankar in the Jain tradition.

facts.text: Vardhaman Mahavir lived from 599 BCE to 527 BCE (birth year 599 BCE).
facts.quote: Vardhaman Mahavir (599 BCE to 527 BCE)

facts.text: Vardhaman Mahavir lived from 599 BCE to 527 BCE (his life ended in 527 BCE).
facts.quote: Vardhaman Mahavir (599 BCE to 527 BCE)

facts.text: The mahajanapada Vrijji (in today's Bihar) had its capital at Vaishali; Mahavir was born in Kundagram, a part of Vaishali.
facts.quote: There was a mahajanapada known as Vrijji in what is known as the State of Bihar today. Its capital was Vaishali. Vardhaman Mahavir was born in Kundagram, a part of Vaishali.

facts.text: Mahavir's father was Siddharth and his mother was Trishala.
facts.quote: His father's name was Siddharth and mother's, Trishala.

facts.text: Mahavir attained enlightenment after twelve and a half years of rigorous 'tapa'; his knowledge was keval, so he is called 'Kevali'.
facts.quote: He attained enlightenment after twelve and a half years of rigorous 'tapa'. This knowledge was pure or keval. Therefore, he is also known as 'Kevali'.

facts.text: Mahavir was called 'Jina' or Conqueror; the term Jain derives from jina.
facts.quote: He was called 'Jina' or Conqueror ... The term Jain derives from the word jina.

facts.text: Mahavir preached for about thirty years in Ardhamagadhi, a people's language.
facts.quote: After the attainment of knowledge, he preached for about thirty years ... he spoke to them in Ardhamagadhi, a people's language.

facts.text: The Tirthankar's preaching assembly, 'Samavasaran', was based on equality; people of all varnas could enter.
facts.quote: The assembly held by the Tirthankar to preach was known as 'Samavasaran' in Ardhamagadhi. Samavasaran was based on equality. People of all varnas had entry to it.

facts.text: The Pancha Mahavratas are Ahimsa (Non-violence), Satya (Truth), Asteya (Non-stealing), Aparigraha (Non-attachment) and Brahmacharya (Chastity).
facts.quote: 1. Ahimsa (Non-violence) ... 2. Satya (Truth) : Every speech and action should be true. 3. Asteya (Non-stealing) ... 4. Aparigraha (Non-attachment) ... 5. Brahmacharya (Chastity)

facts.text: Asteya means not stealing anything; Aparigraha means not hoarding or accumulating anything.
facts.quote: Asteya means 'not stealing' anything. ... Aparigraha means not hoarding or accumulating anything in this way.

facts.text: The Tri-ratna are Samyak Darshan (Right Faith), Samyak Dnyan (Right Knowledge) and Samyak Charitra (Right Conduct); Samyak means 'balanced'.
facts.quote: 1. Samyak Darshan (Right Faith) 2. Samyak Dnyan (Right Knowledge) and 3. Samyak Charitra (Right Conduct) Samyak means 'balanced'.

facts.text: Anekantavada means pluralism or multiple viewpoints; following it builds tolerance towards others' opinions.
facts.quote: Anekantavada is considered to be very important in the quest for truth. It means pluralism or multiple viewpoints. ... If people follow this, they develop tolerance towards the opinions of other people

facts.text: Mahavir taught that greatness depends on conduct, not varna; he gave women the right of sanyas; he taught 'Live and let live'.
facts.quote: the greatness of a human being does not depend on his varna, but on his excellent conduct. ... Vardhaman Mahavir gave the right of sanyas (the right to renounce the world) to women, too. His teachings were: 'Love all living things', 'Have mercy and compassion' and 'Live and let live'.

facts.text: Gautama Buddha lived from 563 BCE to 483 BCE (birth year 563 BCE).
facts.quote: Gautama Buddha (563 BCE To 483 BCE)

facts.text: Gautama Buddha lived from 563 BCE to 483 BCE (his life ended in 483 BCE).
facts.quote: Gautama Buddha (563 BCE To 483 BCE)

facts.text: Gautama Buddha was born at Lumbini in Nepal; father Shuddhodana, mother Mayadevi; birth name Siddharth.
facts.quote: Gautama Buddha was born at Lumbini in Nepal. His father's name was Shuddhodana and mother's name was Mayadevi. His birth name was Siddharth.

facts.text: On Vaishakha Purnima, meditating under a pipal tree at Uruvela near Gaya in Bihar, he attained 'Bodhi'; the tree is the Bodhivriksha and Uruvela is now Bodhgaya.
facts.quote: On Vaishakha Purnima, he was sitting in deep meditation under a pipal tree at Uruvela near the city of Gaya in Bihar. That is when he attained 'Bodhi' ... The tree is now known as the 'Bodhi' tree (Bodhivriksha) and the place Uruvela is known as Bodhgaya.

facts.text: He delivered his first sermon at Sarnath near Varanasi: dhamma-chakka pavattan in Pali, dharma-chakra pravartan in Sanskrit.
facts.quote: He delivered his first sermon at Sarnath near Varanasi. His teachings in the first sermon are termed dhamma. ... this event is called dhamma-chakka pavattan in Pali and dharma-chakra pravartan in Sanskrit.

facts.text: He travelled on foot (charika) for nearly forty-five years and preached in the people's language, Pali.
facts.quote: Later, he travelled on foot (charika) for nearly forty-five years to preach dhamma. He preached in the people's language, Pali.

facts.text: Taking refuge in Buddha, Dhamma and Sangha is called Trisharan.
facts.quote: In Buddhism, the concept of taking refuge in Buddha, Dhamma and Sangha is important. It is known as Trisharan.

facts.text: The four Aryasatyas (Noble Truths): Dukkha, the Cause of Dukkha, Dukkha-nivaran and Pratipad ('the way'), the Ashtangik Marg or Eight-fold Path.
facts.quote: 1. Dukkha (Suffering) ... 2. The Cause of Dukkha ... 3. Dukkha-nivaran : It is possible to end suffering. 4. Pratipad : Pratipad means the 'way'. ... It is known as the Ashtangik Marg or Eight-fold Path.

facts.text: Panchasheel: stay away from killing animals, stealing, unethical conduct, telling lies and intoxicants.
facts.quote: 1. Stay away from killing animals. 2. Stay away from stealing. 3. Stay away from unethical conduct. 4. Stay away from telling lies. 5. Stay away from intoxicants.

facts.text: Followers who entered the sangha were bhikkhus; the separate sangha of women were bhikkhunis; people of all varnas and castes could embrace Buddhism.
facts.quote: Followers who gave up their domestic life and entered the sangha were called bhikkhus. ... There was a separate sangha of women. They are called bhikkhunis. People of all varnas and castes could embrace Buddhism.

facts.text: The Eightfold Path includes Samyak Drishti (Right View), Samyak Vacha (Right speech), Samyak Aajiv (Right livelihood) and Samyak Samadhi (Right concentration).
facts.quote: 1. Samyak Drishti (Right View) ... 3. Samyak Vacha (Right speech) ... 5. Samyak Aajiv (Right livelihood) ... 8. Samyak Samadhi (Right concentration)

facts.text: Buddha's quote 'Even the little quail can chirp freely in her nest' shows his values of freedom and equality; he opposed the rituals of yajna.
facts.quote: One of his famous quotes is that 'Even the little quail can chirp freely in her nest'. This shows his thinking on the values of freedom and equality. ... He opposed the rituals of yajna.

facts.text: Lokayat or Charvak emphasised independent thought and rejected the authority of the Vedas.
facts.quote: The ancient trend of thought known as Lokayat or Charvak is also important. It emphasized on independent thought and rejected the authority of the Vedas.

facts.text: Jewish people may have arrived in Kochi in Kerala around the first to third century CE; the Torah is their important text and the Synagogue their prayer house.
facts.quote: People belonging to the Jewish religion may have arrived in Kochi in Kerala around the first to third century of the Christian Era. ... 'Torah' is an important religious text of Jews ... Their prayer house is known as a 'Synagogue'.

facts.text: Christianity was founded by Jesus Christ; St. Thomas, one of the 12 disciples of Christ, came to Kerala in the first century CE.
facts.quote: Christianity is a religion founded by Jesus Christ. ... St. Thomas, one of the 12 disciples of Christ, came to Kerala in the first century of the Christian Era.

facts.text: St. Thomas established a church at Pallayur in Trichur district in 52 CE.
facts.quote: He established a church at Pallayur in Trichur district, in 52 CE.

facts.text: Christianity teaches that we should love everyone including our enemies and forgive those who err; the Bible is its holy book and the Church its prayer house.
facts.quote: We should love everyone including our enemies. We should forgive those who err or go wrong. The 'Bible' is the holy book of Christianity and their prayerhouse is known as a 'Church'.

facts.text: Islam is monotheistic; the word Islam means peace and also surrender to Allah; its holy book is the Quran Sharif.
facts.quote: Islam is a monotheistic religion. There is only one Allah and Muhammad is his Prophet. The message of God is revealed through him in the holy book of 'Quran' Sharif. The word Islam means peace. It also means surrender to Allah.

facts.text: Islam spread in Arabia in the 7th century CE and arrived in India in the same century through Arab traders; its prayer house is the Masjid (Mosque).
facts.quote: Islam spread in Arabia in the 7th century CE. Islam arrived in India in the same century through the Arab traders. The prayer house of Islam is known as a 'Masjid' (Mosque).

facts.text: The sacred text of the Parsees is the Avesta; the language of the Rigveda and Avesta shows similarities.
facts.quote: The sacred text of the Parsees or Zoroastrian people is the 'Avesta'. The language of the Rigveda and Avesta shows similarlities.

facts.text: The Parsees came from the Pars or Fars province of Iran and are mostly believed to have first come to Gujarat in the eighth century CE.
facts.quote: The Parsees came to India from the Pars or Fars province of Iran. Therefore, they are known as Parsees. It is mostly believed that they first came to Gujarat in the eighth century CE.

facts.text: Zarathushtra or Zoroaster founded the religion; their God is 'Ahur Mazda'; fire and water are very important; the sacred fire burns in the Agyari.
facts.quote: Zarathushtra or Zoroaster was the founder of their religion. 'Ahur Mazda' is the name of their God. The elements of fire and water are very important in their religion. The sacred fire burns in the temples which are known as 'Agyari'.

facts.text: Parsee philosophy rests on good thoughts, good words and good deeds.
facts.quote: At the core of Parsee philosophy are three main principles of conduct, namely, good thoughts, good words and good deeds.

facts.text: 'Ekam Sat Vipraha Bahudha Vadanti' means 'Truth is One. The Wise Call It by Many Names'.
facts.quote: The famous saying 'Ekam Sat Vipraha Bahudha Vadanti' (Truth is One. The Wise Call It by Many Names) is deeply rooted in Indian culture.
